name: Bettermode
tagline: Publish a branded community portal with spaces, posts, and member profiles

pricing.notes: Typical Starter monthly amount; vendor packaging may vary.

verdictSummary: The core loop is buildable, but a dependable replacement becomes a real weekend or multi-day project. For Bettermode, publish a branded community portal with spaces, posts, and member profiles. The hard boundary is embeds, apis, customization, analytics, moderation, and enterprise integrations, plus network, moderation, and communication infrastructure.
coreLoopDIY: Host a branded community portal with spaces, posts, and member profiles, organize discussion into channels or topics, and keep membership and moderation under the owner's control.
whatYouLose: embeds, APIs, customization, analytics, moderation, and enterprise integrations
ongoingBurden: realtime delivery, notifications, abuse handling, search, media, permissions, mobile clients, backups, and community operations
whyPeopleStillPay: People still pay for Bettermode because community software is valuable when members are already there and the operator does not have to own realtime reliability and abuse response. The recurring cost buys realtime delivery, notifications, abuse handling, search, media, permissions, mobile clients, backups, and community operations, not just the visible interface.

priorArt.name: Discourse
priorArt.desc: Mature open-source community discussion platform with strong moderation and search.

alternatives.name: Discourse
alternatives.desc: Forums, chat and member profiles with a decade of battle scars; Ruby, Postgres and Redis become your hobbies.

facts.install: Use official paid hosting, or run the supported Docker-based production install on a Linux server with a domain and SMTP
facts.dataFormat: Topics, posts, users, and settings live in PostgreSQL, transient state in Redis, and uploads on local disk or S3-compatible storage; admins can create full backups.
facts.gapVsPaid: Discourse is mature and powerful, but it remains forum-first, requires a Ruby/PostgreSQL/Redis stack, and lacks Bettermode's no-code branded portal and business modules.
facts.setupBlocker: The free route starts with a Linux server, root access, DNS, SMTP, Docker, backups, security updates, and ongoing moderation configuration.

alternatives.name: Flarum
alternatives.desc: The least baroque forum here; extensions arrive before courses, events or payments.

facts.install: Install the release archive or Composer package on PHP with MySQL/MariaDB and a configured web server
facts.dataFormat: Discussions, users, and extension data live in the SQL database; avatars and uploaded assets live on the server filesystem or extension-provided storage.
facts.gapVsPaid: Flarum is lean and attractive, but much of the community experience depends on extensions and there is no built-in equivalent to Bettermode's courses, events, payments, or portal builder.
facts.setupBlocker: A non-expert must already know PHP hosting, Composer, database credentials, file permissions, cron, and web-server rewrites, and the current 1.x line is receiving only critical and security fixes while 2.0 matures.

alternatives.name: Forem
alternatives.desc: A branded publishing community with profiles, feeds and discussion; deployment is considerably less friendly than the members.

facts.install: Deploy the current beta production setup with Kamal 2, Docker, a registry, SSH access, PostgreSQL, Redis, and a domain
facts.dataFormat: Profiles, articles, comments, and relationships live in PostgreSQL; cache/jobs use Redis, while uploaded media uses the configured file or cloud-media backend.
facts.gapVsPaid: Forem delivers profiles, feeds, publishing, and discussion, but it is publishing-first and its beta production deployment is far less approachable than Bettermode's hosted builder.
facts.setupBlocker: The project's own production deployment path is explicitly beta and assumes comfort with Docker images, Kamal, SSH, secrets, a registry, PostgreSQL, Redis, DNS, and backups.

alternatives.name: HumHub
alternatives.desc: Spaces, profiles, streams and events on your server; payments and courses are not hiding in a submenu.

facts.install: Use HumHub's paid hosted service, or install the Community Edition PHP package on a web server with MySQL/MariaDB
facts.dataFormat: Profiles, spaces, posts, and configuration live in the HumHub SQL database; uploaded files live under the instance's uploads directory or configured storage.
facts.gapVsPaid: HumHub supplies spaces, profiles, streams, and events, but server administration and weaker mobile polish are the cost, while courses and payments usually require separate or premium modules.
facts.setupBlocker: The free route needs a PHP server, database, web-server configuration, cron jobs, mail delivery, backups, and upgrades before the first member joins.

alternatives.name: NodeBB
alternatives.desc: A fast modern forum with profiles and real-time chat; MongoDB, Redis or Postgres becomes your problem.

facts.install: Buy NodeBB hosting, or clone/install the Node.js app and run its setup against MongoDB, Redis, or PostgreSQL; Docker Compose is also available
facts.dataFormat: Users, posts, sessions, and plugin data live in the selected database; uploaded assets live on disk or a configured storage plugin/backend.
facts.gapVsPaid: NodeBB is a fast modern forum with profiles and real-time discussion, but it remains forum-first and lacks Bettermode's no-code portal layouts, packaged spaces, courses, and monetization.
facts.setupBlocker: The self-hosted path requires a supported Node.js runtime, database choice and maintenance, reverse proxy/TLS, email, process supervision, backups, and plugin-compatible upgrades.

notes: Editorial comparison targets the Starter plan and a single private community DIY substitute. Recheck price before merge.
prompt:
Build a personal replacement for Bettermode in an empty repository.
Use Next.js 15, TypeScript, PostgreSQL, Drizzle ORM, WebSockets, and Docker Compose; do not offer alternative stacks.
The core loop is: host a branded community portal with spaces, posts, and member profiles, organize discussion into channels or topics, and keep membership and moderation under the owner's control.
Make the first run work locally with one documented command.
Store all user data locally by default and make export straightforward.
Put secrets in .env, ship .env.example, and never commit credentials.
Implement spaces, channels, topics, replies, reactions, mentions, profiles, roles, and invitations.
Use WebSockets for live updates but preserve every message transactionally in PostgreSQL.
Add moderation queues, reports, blocks, rate limits, attachment limits, and an audit log.
Provide email digests, browser notifications, search, pinned content, and member export.
Add owner-controlled retention, account deletion, backup, restore, and health checks.
Ship Docker Compose with a seeded demo, migrations, and an emergency admin command.
Include clear empty, loading, success, and recoverable error states.
Add input validation, safe filenames, and graceful handling of unavailable APIs.
Write focused tests for the core transformation and one end-to-end happy path.
Create a README with setup, architecture, permissions, data location, and backup steps.
Do not add accounts, billing, telemetry, analytics, or a hosted control plane.
Deliberately leave out public-network discovery and existing member liquidity.
Deliberately leave out production voice or video rooms.
Deliberately leave out native mobile applications, enterprise SSO, and 24-hour abuse operations.
Finish by running the tests and listing the exact commands used.
